title: [finding] `packages/client-react/.examples-build/` is not gitignored — check:skill-examples' second surface writes an untracked throwaway dir
body:
Found while adding a third surface to `check:skill-examples` (#10924 / PR #11433). Filed, not folded: that PR adds the `.gitignore` entry for the surface it introduces, but this is a pre-existing gap from a different card and a different path.

## The gap

`check-skill-examples.ts` writes each surface's extracted blocks to a throwaway dir under that surface's `resolutionDir`. `.gitignore` covers only spec's:

```
# Throwaway build dir for `check:skill-examples` (extracted skill code blocks)
packages/spec/.examples-build/
```

#10969 added the client SDK surface, whose `resolutionDir` is `packages/client-react` (it needs react's real types, which pnpm does not hoist). That surface therefore writes `packages/client-react/.examples-build/`, and nothing ignores it — measured: `grep -n examples-build .gitignore` returns exactly one line, and neither `packages/client-react/.gitignore` nor `packages/spec/.gitignore` exists.

## Why it is worth an entry rather than a shrug

The gate removes the dir on exit, so it is invisible on a clean run — which is precisely what makes it a trap rather than noise:

- `--keep` is a documented debug flag (`tsx scripts/check-skill-examples.ts --keep`) whose whole purpose is to leave the dir for inspection. Using it on the client surface leaves ~19 extracted `.tsx` files showing as untracked.
- A run interrupted before cleanup (the container SIGTERMs a foreground command at ~10 minutes) leaves the same residue.
- In either state a `git add -A` — which agents in this repo run routinely — commits the extracted blocks into someone's PR. Duplicated example code landing in `packages/client-react/` would be confusing to every later reader, and the copies are stale by construction.

The spec entry exists for exactly these reasons; the second surface just never got one.

## Fix

One line beside the existing entry, and the comment above it generalised to say there is one dir per surface:

```
packages/client-react/.examples-build/
```

PR #11433 does the same for the surface it adds, and also asserts at runtime that no two surfaces resolve to the same build dir — but nothing asserts that each declared dir is ignored, so this class stays hand-maintained. A gate for that (walk `SURFACES`, check each build dir against `git check-ignore`) is a reasonable but larger option, worth deciding rather than assuming.
